key_insight: SGD in a two-layer ReLU network learns the shortcut spurious feature before the true XOR signal, and the spurious component can suppress later signal learning.
engineering_relevance: This shows why models can lock onto easy correlations during training, highlighting the need for robustness checks and mitigation strategies in high-dimensional learning systems.
method: Analyze online minibatch SGD on a two-layer ReLU network trained with logistic loss
Use a Boolean hypercube data model with XOR signal plus linear spurious correlation
Derive phase-based learning dynamics and identify when spurious alignment dominates
evidence_signal: Theoretical analysis on a synthetic XOR-plus-spurious data model, with preliminary empirical evidence that the XOR signal may emerge later when spurious correlation is only constant.
watch_item: Results are for an idealized synthetic setting, so real-world behavior may differ when data, architecture, or optimization details change.
paper_title: SGD Provably Prioritizes a Shortcut Spurious Feature in the XOR Model
